g.text: A word is cut into overlapping character windows. Each word is padded with a space first, so word edges are distinct from the middle.

g.text: Partial typing works the same way. nordi produces 9 grams, 7 of which sit inside Nordic. So a search box gives useful results while the user is still typing.

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Spacing stops mattering. Someone types solar winds, the snapshot says SolarWinds. Word-level search finds nothing. Grams overlap heavily, so it lands. That is test_a_name_split_in_two_still_matches.

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Padding is the detail that makes it correct. ' no' is a prefix gram. Without the pad, nor inside Senorita would score the same as Nordic. The pad keeps "starts with" separate from "contains".

g.text: Why n-grams only on the name

Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: match_gram_parts = ["name"]. Location and sector are deliberately excluded.

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Those two are short controlled lists. Grams blur their values together — india and australia share the gram ia , Materials and Utilities share ties. On a list of 20 countries that noise is worse than the typo tolerance is worth. So location and business are matched on whole words.

Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Name is different. It is free text, high cardinality, and the thing people mistype.

Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Why BM25 and not just "count the shared grams"

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Plain overlap counting fails in three ways. BM25 fixes each one.

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: │ Problem │ What plain counting does │ What BM25 does │

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: │ Common grams │ ing, ion, co appear in thousands of names and dominate the count │ IDF weights them near zero, rare grams like rwi carry the match │

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: │ Repeated grams │ a name repeating a gram five times scores 5x │ k1 = 1.5 saturates it — the 2nd occurrence adds much less than the 1st │

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: │ Long names │ long names accumulate more grams and win by sheer length │ b normalises by document length │

Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: score = IDF(t) × ( f(t,d) × (k1 + 1) ) / ( f(t,d) + k1 × (1 − b + b × len(d)/avg_len) )

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: The b value is the tuned one. It is 0.5, not the textbook 0.75 — app/services/matching.py:47. Reason:

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Both contain every gram of capgemini. At b = 0.75 the longer one is punished for being long and drops below. At 0.5 they stay comparable. This was not a taste call — scripts/eval_match.py measures 0.5 as better than 0.75 on every query style.

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: k1 = 1.5 is the standard value, left alone.

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Why not embeddings for the name

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: An embedding captures meaning. A company name has no meaning to capture — SolarWinds is a label, not a concept. You want the string matched as written. Embeddings would happily pull in "other solar companies", which is wrong for a name lookup.

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji
Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: The opposite holds for business_model. "network monitoring software" shares no word with "Systems Software", so BM25 alone cannot connect them. That is the one part where embeddings earn their place, at match_semantic_weight = 0.6.

g.text: - Name 0.50 — it is the only part that identifies one company. Sector and country identify a group. If someone types a name, that is the strongest intent signal they can give.

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Business 0.35 — narrows from thousands to a few hundred. Real discriminating power, but never unique.

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Location 0.15 — weakest. AMER covers a huge share of the snapshot. Given more weight it would start pulling wrong companies to the top just for sharing a country. It is a filter-ish signal, not an identifying one.
